source.stem:
Multiple choice questions.

System of equations

$$
\left\{ \begin{array}{l} 3 x + 4 y = 5, \\ - 7 x + 9 y = - \frac {5}{2} \end{array} \right.
$$

The solution is ( ).

(A) $\left\{ \begin{array}{l}x = 2,\\ y = -0.25 \end{array} \right.$

(B) $\left\{ \begin{array}{l}x = -5.5,\\ y = 4 \end{array} \right.$

(C) $\left\{ \begin{array}{l}x = 1,\\ y = 0.5 \end{array} \right.$

(D) $\left\{ \begin{array}{l}x = -1,\\ y = -0.5 \end{array} \right.$

mx.teacher_note: common factor still holds here even though A jump size that reaches only one of the two numbers, such as 7 for 14 and 36, does not is missing from the stem — on the item about Decide which single jump sizes can reach two treasure.

mx.teacher_note: Reaches both treasures is what produces factor of the first number and factor of the second number, so the usual direction of this relation is run backwards — on the item about Decide which single jump sizes can reach two treasure.

mx.name: scope_error
mx.teacher_note: The common factor rule also covers this: jump sizes that hit only one treasure, so it is not an exception — on the item about Decide which single jump sizes can reach two treasure.

mx.name: mechanism_conflation
mx.teacher_note: common factor is settled by running 'Recognize when two prime factorisations are the same despite a': A number has only one prime factorisation except for the order of the prime factors — on the item about Decide which single jump sizes can reach two treasure.

intelligence.enrichment: A single jump size reaches two treasure numbers exactly when it is a factor of both numbers; the successful shared jump sizes are the common factors.
